title: Can I MASTER Petrified Chess?
summary: chess.com Petrified Chess vs online humans (~1470-1550): pieces turn to stone on capture, pawns can move sideways, and the winner is whoever has the most points from captured pieces (checkmate is worth 20). Goal: win five games. He learns that capturing a non-pawn piece petrifies YOUR capturing piece (so Qxb? loses the queen into a stone) - there are no truly fair trades - and that kings can't capture. Fifth win comes in game 6.
rules: When a piece captures an enemy NON-pawn piece, the capturing piece turns to stone: it stays on that square as a permanent, immovable, uncapturable obstacle (grey stone piece). Capturing a pawn does not petrify the capturer (1:30 'if I take this bishop... the queen turns to stone'; 0:20 'Pawns don't turn into stones. So that's just a free point').
The capturer's side scores the captured piece's value (P1, N3, B3, R5, Q9); the side that loses a piece to a petrifying capture scores nothing for the stone.
Kings cannot capture (4:10 'kings can't take anything actually').
Pawns may also move one square sideways.
Checkmate awards 20 points and ends the game; otherwise the game ends (e.g. no moves/resign/flag) and most points wins.
Tactic: a piece giving adjacent check that must be captured (king can't take) works like mate since capturing it petrifies the taker.
win_condition: Most points at game end (checkmate = +20). Series goal: 5 wins (5th in game 6).

board.shape_notes: standard 8x8; stones act as permanent blocked squares

current_impl_issues: Legacy 'petrified' freezes a random piece each turn and requires checkmate - wrong. Real rules: capturer petrifies when taking non-pawns, points race, kings can't capture, sideways pawns, mate = +20.
